approach_variants.name: Waptus River and the PCT, then the Shovel Creek fisherman's trail to the foot of the slab
approach_variants.notes:
From the Salmon La Sac trailhead, hike the Waptus River Trail about nine miles to Waptus Lake. The bridge has been out, so wade or rock-hop the river at the horse ford. Where the trail joins the PCT, head southbound (west).

Shortly before the PCT crosses the Waptus River, leave the trail and head northwest toward a faint shoulder and bench through flat, easy forest. Pick up a fisherman's trail on the southwest side of that bench and follow it toward Shovel Creek, then up and over the bench past an informal campsite with a giant cairn, where it starts to climb the shoulder on the east side of Shovel Creek.

Before long the trail leaves the forest straight onto talus. Easy talus walking brings you to Shovel Creek; cross where convenient.

Roughly 13 miles to the base, five to six hours. Most parties camp near the Waptus River PCT bridge.
approach_variants.season: July to September; documented ascents cluster in August
hazards: About 2,000 ft of unprotected friction slab, mostly climbed unroped
Rock quality deteriorating markedly on the final three summit-block pitches
No water on the slab — carry the whole climbing day's supply
A long, remote approach with no confirmed cell coverage
The Shovel Lake descent alternative involves loose dirt high, brush and cliff bands low, and heavy route-finding
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Crossing Shovel Creek off the talus puts you at the foot of the Mega Slab — that is the arrival, and it is a creek crossing rather than a judgement. The slab drops from the peak's southeast shoulder at about 6,700 ft all the way to Shovel Creek at about 3,700 ft, so there is no ambiguity about which piece of rock it is: it is the enormous unbroken sheet above you, one of the longest continuous sandstone slabs in North America.

Which line on the slab is the real question here, and for this route the answer is a single word: lowest. Infinite Beauty begins at the lowest part of the slab, on a shallow rib. Walk the base downhill until it stops going down, and start on the rib there.

How that distinguishes it from its neighbour: Timeless Treasure climbs the middle of the slab. So if you have walked out along the base looking for a nicer-looking start, you are on Timeless Treasure. The lowest point is the whole distinction and it is decidable by walking downhill rather than by looking.

What the rock should feel like, as confirmation: clean, solid, grippy low-angle stone with minimal breaks, and roughly 2,000 ft of sustained fourth class. Approach shoes or trail runners friction well on it and most of the slab is climbed unroped. If you are pulling into cracks or dodging vegetation, you are off the clean sheet.

And where the route ends its own identity: after about 2,000 ft the line naturally angles right and joins Timeless Treasure for brief, unexposed low-fifth moves up overlaps trending up and right to the southeast shoulder. Easy scrambling then leads to the summit block, where the rock quality noticeably deteriorates over the final three pitches.

waypoints.name: Salmon La Sac Trailhead
waypoints.directions: From I-90 Exit 80, drive through Roslyn and follow SR 903 north past Cle Elum Lake to Salmon La Sac, about 19 miles from Cle Elum. Just before the Salmon La Sac Campground entrance, turn right onto the gravel road to the Salmon La Sac trailhead, shared by the Waptus River and Cooper River trails. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit at the trail.

waypoints.name: Bears Breast Mountain summit (route GPS reference)
waypoints.directions: Hike Waptus River Trail 1310 about 9 miles to Waptus Lake and turn west (southbound) on the PCT toward its Waptus River bridge, where most parties camp. Shortly before the bridge, head northwest to a bench and pick up a faint fisherman's track up the east side of Shovel Creek to talus and the foot of the Mega Slab. Start at the slab's lowest point, climb to the southeast shoulder, then scramble to and climb the three-pitch summit block.
